ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a wireframe cube box, with a solid sphere placed inside; the circular outline of the sphere and the dashed arc lines indicate the complete shape of the sphere, and the dashed edges of the cube indicate the hidden height or depth direction. Reasoning: The problem states that the diameter of the sphere is equal to the height of the box. The box is a cube, with side length 30 cm, so the height of the box is also 30 cm. Therefore the diameter of the sphere is 30 cm, and the radius is 15 cm. The volume of the cube is 30^3=27000 cubic centimeters. The volume of the sphere is (4/3)π(15)^3=(4/3)π·3375=4500π cubic centimeters. The volume in the box not occupied by the sphere is equal to the volume of the cube minus the volume of the sphere, that is, 27000-4500π.

method.method_draft: First read the image as a solid sphere placed inside a wireframe cube; the sphere is the object occupying part of the cube, and the dashed/hidden lines indicate the cube's height/depth and the sphere's full round shape. From the text, use that the cube has edge length 30 cm and that the sphere's diameter equals the box height. Since the box is a cube, its height is also 30 cm, so the sphere radius is 15 cm. Compute cube volume as 30^3=27000 and sphere volume as (4/3)π(15)^3=4500π. The unoccupied volume is cube volume minus sphere volume: 27000-4500π.

method.method_draft: Read the image as showing a sphere whose vertical extent matches the cube's height, so it can be treated as a sphere with diameter equal to one cube edge. From the text, the cube edge length is 30 cm, so let the shared diameter/edge length be s=30. Instead of computing the radius first, use the general comparison: a sphere with diameter s has radius s/2 and volume (4/3)π(s/2)^3=(π/6)s^3. Thus the sphere occupies π/6 of the cube's volume. The cube volume is 30^3=27000, so the unoccupied volume is 27000-(π/6)(27000)=27000-4500π.
